GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
Regional Government is the Situbondo Regency Government.
Regent is the Situbondo Regent.
Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. Violence is any act unlawfully committed, with or without the use of means, against the physical and psychological condition that causes danger to life or body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child, who should be trustworthy, such as parents, close family, teachers and assistants/companions.
Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of impending, ongoing or already occurred violence against victims.
Assistant/Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
10. Integrated Service Center (PPT) for Victims of Violence against Women and Children of Situbondo Regency, hereinafter referred to as PPT Situbondo Regency, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
11. Safe house (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
12. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
13. Woman is a person who is female.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or a father and his children, and a mother and her children.
15. Household is family members and relatives such as grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, husbands, wives, cousins and so forth, and non-relatives such as domestic workers, drivers and so forth who live and reside in one house.
16. Community and Women Empowerment Agency, hereinafter abbreviated as BPMP, is the Community and Women Empowerment Agency of Situbondo Regency.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
The implementation of protection for victims of violence is organized based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must obtain their right to protection for a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which contradicts what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. To achieve integrated and comprehensive Protection services for Women and Children Victims of Violence, an integrated form of service from various related institutions is required, including medical services, medicolegal, psychosocial, legal assistance, accompaniment, economic independence (training). These services are carried out evenly across all levels of society so that every citizen has the right to obtain equal opportunities to receive security and legal protection.
In principle, the strategic target of protection implementation is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and safe and comfortable shelters that are conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through stages that are mutually interrelated, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.
There are four important phenomena that need to be observed in relation to the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence. First, is violence against women and children from year to year the number increases with the mode of violence tending to be more sadistic (perpetrators who slit throats, pour hot water, throw into wells, to breaking parts of limbs and so on). Second, the many cases of violence against Domestic Workers (PRT) dominated by women that have occurred recently require attention from all parties, especially the existence of legal protection, regulations and policies that protect them. Third, the lack of facilities and infrastructure for safe and comfortable shelters that are conducive for victims of violence. These three phenomena indicate the increasing complexity of violent behavior whose victims are dominated by women and children, both those who work as domestic workers and others. Fourth, children are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in them is inherent dignity and worth as complete human beings. Children are the next generation of the nation's struggle ideals who have a strategic role, and have special characteristics and traits that are expected to ensure the continuity of the nation and state's existence in the future. Children need to get the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, cognitively, spiritually and socially.
Due to its nature, children's growth and development must be carried out in an environment that protects from all dangers in the form of optimal care.
Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and firmly giving a mandate to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, the Regional Regulation can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.
The implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence in Situbondo Regency is carried out based on Situbondo Regent Regulation Number 6 of 2006 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Acts of Violence against Women and Children and Situbondo Regent Decree No. 188/237 1P.00 L.2/2007 concerning the Integrated Service Center (PPT) for Victims of Violence against Women and Children in Situbondo Regency. As with the phenomena described above, Regent Regulation Number 6 of 2006 has not yet been able to become a comprehensive legal umbrella in providing protection for women and children victims of violence. With this Regional Regulation, it is expected to anticipate and overcome the conditions of violence occurring in Situbondo Regency, so that it can provide protection and services to victims of violence in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Article 3
Paragraph (1) What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men.
Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by "physical violence" is acts that result in pain, falling ill, or serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting, pulling hair/yanking, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons, and/or causing disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.
Point b What is meant by "psychological violence" is acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or degrading self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.
Point c What is meant by "sexual violence" is violence against sexuality which includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her emotional needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household scope, forced sexual intercourse against one person within their household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
Point d What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or children or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of limiting and/or prohibiting family members from doing decent work.
Point e What is meant by "restriction of movement" is limiting the movement of the wife or children in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting gathering and socializing in the community as well as limiting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

The implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence in Situbondo Regency is carried out based on Situbondo Regent Regulation Number 6 of 2006 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Acts of Violence against Women and Children and Situbondo Regent Decree No. 188/237 1P.00 L.2/2007 concerning the Integrated Service Center (PPT) for Victims of Violence against Women and Children in Situbondo Regency. As with the phenomena described above, Regent Regulation Number 6 of 2006 has not yet been able to become a comprehensive legal umbrella in providing protection for women and children victims of violence. With this Regional Regulation, it is expected to anticipate and overcome the conditions of violence occurring in Situbondo Regency, so that it can provide protection and services to victims of violence in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Article 3
Paragraph (1) What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men.
Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by "physical violence" is acts that result in pain, falling ill, or serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting, pulling hair/yanking, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons, and/or causing disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.
Point b What is meant by "psychological violence" is acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse such as insults, hurtful comments or degrading self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening or intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.
Point c What is meant by "sexual violence" is violence against sexuality which includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her emotional needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction. Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the household scope, forced sexual intercourse against one person within their household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
Point d What is meant by "economic neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife or children or family members or relatives such as not providing for the wife, even spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers and includes acts of limiting and/or prohibiting family members from doing decent work.
Point e What is meant by "restriction of movement" is limiting the movement of the wife or children in developing their potential both for economic and social purposes such as prohibiting gathering and socializing in the community as well as limiting the movement of relatives such as preventing domestic workers or drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
Regional Government is the Situbondo Regency Government.
Regent is the Situbondo Regent.
Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. Violence is any act unlawfully committed, with or without the use of means, against the physical and psychological condition that causes danger to life or body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child, who should be trustworthy, such as parents, close family, teachers and assistants/companions.
Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of impending, ongoing or already occurred violence against victims.
Assistant/Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
10. Integrated Service Center (PPT) for Victims of Violence against Women and Children of Situbondo Regency, hereinafter referred to as PPT Situbondo Regency, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
11. Safe house (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
12. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
13. Woman is a person who is female.
14. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or a father and his children, and a mother and her children.
15. Household is family members and relatives such as grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, husbands, wives, cousins and so forth, and non-relatives such as domestic workers, drivers and so forth who live and reside in one house.
16. Community and Women Empowerment Agency, hereinafter abbreviated as BPMP, is the Community and Women Empowerment Agency of Situbondo Regency.

Article 14
Supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of violence (1) is carried out by BPMP.
In conducting supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), BPMP has the authority to:
a. place victims of violence in a safe house;
b. summon and present the family of victims of violence to be heard for their statement; and
c. order PPT to provide protection to a person who is a victim of violence.
(3) BPMP is obligated to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of protection for women and children who are victims of violence.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "the principle of respect for human rights" is that the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is to guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of victims of violence as a manifestation of respect for human rights.
Letter b What is meant by "the principle of gender equality and justice" is a process of equality and conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social and cultural activities, national defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of such development.
Letter c What is meant by "the principle of protection of victims' rights" is protection of the person, family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, a sense of security and protection from threats of fear, and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.
Letter d What is meant by "the non-discriminatory principle" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
Letter e What is meant by "the principle of the best interests of the victim" is that in all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Article 13
The family and/or parents as referred to in Article 10 letter c and letter d have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 12
The responsibility of the community as referred to in Article 10 letter b is implemented in the form of:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children; and
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties.

CHAPTER VII
FINANCING
Article 15
(1) Financing for the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be charged to the Regional Budget of Situbondo Regency and other lawful sources.
(2) Budget management for the implementation of protection for victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of fairness, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

CHAPTER VIII
CRIMINAL PROVISIONS
Article 16
Any person who deliberately allows violence against women and children to occur and/or does not report the occurrence of violence against women and children, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 17
(1) Any person who intentionally violates the provisions as referred to in Article 6 paragraph (3), shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of at most Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).
(2) In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to carry out protection, shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).
(3) Organizers or managers of PPT or Safe Houses who are proven to violate the provisions as referred to in Article 9 paragraph (2), shall be punished with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Article 6
(1) The safe house as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (1) provides a place and/or temporary safe shelter for victims of violence until their rights are restored.
(2) The operation and/or management of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by PPT.
(3) For security and at the request of the victim of violence, the manager or operator of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (2) may place the victim of violence in a certain location that is kept confidential.

(1) In the event that victims of violence as referred to in Article 4 require continuous handling, they have the right to stay in a safe house or alternative residence.
(2) Continuous handling as referred to in paragraph (1) constitutes handling at the rehabilitation stage carried out by individuals, groups or Government and non-Government institutions.

6.11.rationale: The original Indonesian text does explicitly mention domestic workers (PRT) in a way that connects to protection needs: in the PENJELASAN UMUM it states “banyaknya kasus kekerasan terhadap Pekerja Rumah Tangga (PRT) ... membutuhkan perhatian ... terlebih adanya perlindungan hukum, peraturan dan kebijakan yang melindungi mereka.” Also, in the detailed explanation of Pasal 3 ayat (2) huruf d (penelantaran ekonomi), it explicitly includes “tidak memberikan atau menahan gaji pekerja rumah tangga maupun sopir” (withholding wages of domestic workers/drivers) as a form of violence. This latter point is shown to the judge in [6.11-34]. Given the indicator “Domestic workers,” this is direct textual inclusion of domestic workers within the violence/protection framing. The judge’s rationale (“only background, no specific measures”) overlooks that the regulation’s definitional/explanatory section explicitly references domestic workers as potential victims/affected persons, so the error is primarily a misread/overly narrow evaluation despite available evidence.
